statement: In BLIS, always-disaggregate (AD) yields consistently lower mean inter-token latency (ITL) than always-local (AL) across all tested arrival rates (10-150 req/s), with the ITL advantage growing monotonically from 0.13ms at rate=10 to 1.69ms at rate=150, then saturating near 1.69ms. The advantage is absent at rate=1 (batch size=1).
regime: qwen/qwen3-14b, 4 instances (2 prefill + 2 decode), 512 prompt tokens, 128 output tokens, 300 requests, rates 1-150 req/s, seeds 42-46
mechanism: AD separates prefill from decode across instance types, allowing decode-only instances to batch with larger B. ITL = F/B + c per decode step; AD's dedicated decode instances have larger effective B than AL's shared instances. At rate=1, no overlap between requests (B=1 always), so no advantage. Advantage saturates when B stops growing with rate (near rate=130-150).
applicability_bounds: Holds for 2 prefill + 2 decode PD split with least-loaded routing. The saturation near 1.69ms corresponds to maximum B achievable at 150 req/s. Zero difference at rate=1 is exact (deterministic token lengths eliminate stochastic variation).

statement: In BLIS, both AL and AD ITL follow a concave, monotonically increasing function of arrival rate described by ITL = a + b·rate/(1+d·rate) (R² > 0.996 for AL, > 0.998 for AD across 5 seeds). The paper's M/G/1-derived model α/(1−λW) achieves R² < 0.12 (AL) and R² < 0.56 (AD) — far below expected. The corrected model's MAE is 11x lower than the paper model's. Cross-validation confirms the corrected model generalizes to unseen rates (mean CV AE = 0.19ms for AL, 0.10ms for AD vs 1.66ms and 0.92ms for paper model). All results are statistically robust across 5 seeds (per-seed R² std < 8e-6).
regime: qwen/qwen3-14b, 4 instances (2P+2D), 512/128 tokens, 300 requests, rates 1-150 req/s, seeds 42-46 (5 seeds)
mechanism: The step-time formula (sim/latency/trained_physics_model.go:321-328) contains fixed per-step costs (β₅·L=1284µs, β₇=126µs, β₃·tWeight) that are amortized over batch size B. As arrival rate increases, continuous batching grows B, so per-token ITL decelerates toward an asymptote (concave shape). The paper model treats α as constant (B-independent), producing a convex curve that systematically overshoots at low rates and undershoots at high rates — an S-shaped residual pattern that cannot be fixed by any parameter choice. The corrected model's rational form a + b·rate/(1+d·rate) is concave for d>0, matching the data's physical shape.
applicability_bounds: R² values are nearly seed-invariant (std < 8e-6) because deterministic token lengths (stdev=0) make mean ITL dominated by batching dynamics, not arrival jitter. Cross-validation shows corrected model advantage is strongest at high rates (rate>50) where shape mismatch grows. Paper model wins LOOCV at rates 20-30 where convex and concave curves happen to nearly intersect.

statement: In BLIS with deterministic token lengths (stdev=0) and 300 requests, ITL model fit quality (R²) is effectively seed-invariant: the corrected model's per-seed R² standard deviation is < 8e-6 across 5 seeds for both AL and AD modes. The paper model's R² is also nearly constant across seeds (std < 0.0015) but consistently poor. This seed-invariance confirms that mean ITL at each rate is determined by batching dynamics, not Poisson arrival jitter.
regime: qwen/qwen3-14b, 4 instances (2P+2D), 512/128 tokens stdev=0, 300 requests, seeds 42-46
mechanism: With zero token-length variance, each request has identical computation requirements. The only source of randomness is Poisson arrival timing. With 300 requests and 12ms mean ITL per step, mean ITL is a time-average over thousands of decode steps — the variance of a Poisson time-average decreases as O(1/√n). The corrected model's per-seed parameter stability (a varies by ±0.0003, b by ±0.00004, d by ±0.000012 across seeds) directly reflects this near-determinism.
applicability_bounds: Applies specifically to stdev=0 workloads. Variable token lengths (stdev > 0) would introduce additional seed-to-seed variance in ITL curves, potentially reducing seed-invariance of R² estimates.

statement: In BLIS, always-disaggregate (AD) incurs consistently higher mean TTFT than always-local (AL) across all tested arrival rates, with a penalty of 4.2-9.4ms due to KV transfer overhead (~3.4ms at 25 GB/s) plus prefill server queueing.
mechanism: AD requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode instance before decode can begin, adding ~3.4ms constant transfer cost at 25 GB/s plus additional prefill queue waiting time that grows with rate.
applicability_bounds: Applies at 25 GB/s KV transfer bandwidth. Different bandwidths would scale the constant term proportionally.
